docs.title: Home
docs.text: A fluent, thread-safe Go image processing library with chainable operations.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Fluent Interface: Chain multiple operations together naturally
  • Thread-Safe: Individually synchronized methods; multi-call chains are not atomic
  • High-Quality Processing: Uses Catmull-Rom interpolation for resizing
  • Comprehensive Error Handling: Errors propagate through the chain
  • Multiple Format Support: JPEG and PNG input/output; GIF input (decode-only)
  • Text Watermarks: Add customizable text overlays with font control

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/TamasGorgics/gopiq

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "os"

    "github.com/TamasGorgics/gopiq"
)

func main() {
    imageData, err := os.ReadFile("img.jpg")
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Error reading image: %v\n", err)
        return
    }

    // Load and process an image with method chaining
    processor := gopiq.FromBytes(imageData).
        Resize(800, 600).
        Grayscale().
        Crop(100, 100, 400, 300).
        AddTextWatermark("© 2025",
            gopiq.WithFontSize(24),
            gopiq.WithPosition(gopiq.PositionBottomRight))

    if processor.Err() != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Error: %v\n", processor.Err())
        return
    }

    // Export the result
    resultBytes, err := processor.ToBytes(gopiq.FormatJPEG)
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Export error: %v\n", err)
        return
    }

    err = os.WriteFile("output.jpg", resultBytes, 0644)
    if err != nil {
        fmt.Printf("Error writing output file: %v\n", err)
        return
    }

    fmt.Println("Image processed and saved successfully")
}

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
The module has one public package and one implementation package:

github.com/TamasGorgics/gopiq          # public API
github.com/TamasGorgics/gopiq/internal/engine

The root package owns the exported API: ImageProcessor, formats, performance options, and watermark options. The engine owns image state, synchronization, decoding/encoding, and image processing. Engine types are intentionally not used in public function signatures.

docs.title: Dependency direction
docs.text:
• The root package may import internal/engine.
  • internal/engine must not import the root package.
  • Examples import only the root package.
  • A future cmd/gopiq CLI must import only the root package. It may use internal/cli for command logic, but not internal/engine.

The internal directory prevents external modules from importing the engine. Packages inside this module can still import it, so the dependency rule is enforced by review and can later be checked with a linter.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• Root-package tests exercise behavior through the facade, and api_test.go compiles against the public package as an external consumer.
  • internal/engine tests cover implementation details such as checked arithmetic, worker counts, fixed-point conversion, and decoding/encoding helpers.
  • The coverage command includes both the root package and the engine.

docs.title: Planned CLI
docs.text: The CLI will live under cmd/gopiq, with testable command logic under internal/cli. It will use FromBytes, the chainable operations, and ToBytes from the public package. This keeps the CLI a consumer of the same API that external applications use.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: gopiq synchronizes individual method calls. Image, Err, ToBytes, and Clone take read locks; processing methods and SetPerformanceOptions take write locks. The processor state and its image reference can therefore be accessed safely from multiple goroutines.

docs.title: Chains are not atomic
docs.text:
A multi-call chain is not an atomic transaction. Another goroutine may interleave between calls in a chain, so the image seen by the next call is not guaranteed to be the result of the previous call in your goroutine. Use separate processors or an external mutex when an entire sequence must be atomic.

proc := gopiq.New(image)

// Another goroutine may run between these calls; this is not one atomic step.
proc.Resize(800, 600).Crop(10, 10, 200, 200).Grayscale()

docs.title: Read-only images
docs.text:
New retains the image passed to it. Image() returns the processor's current image. Treat both as read-only while the processor or any clone may be used concurrently.

Processing operations do not modify their source in place; for non-empty images they create a new destination image. This is what allows clones to process a shared source independently. Mutating an image through a concrete-type assertion is outside the thread-safety guarantee.

source := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, 800, 600))
proc := gopiq.New(source)

// Do not call source.Set while proc or its clones are in use.
_, err := proc.Resize(400, 300).Image()
if err != nil {
    // Handle the error.
}
// Any image obtained from Image is read-only too.

docs.title: Clone is shallow
docs.text:
Clone creates a shallow copy of the processor. It copies the current error and performance options, but shares the current image reference and its pixel storage with the original. Clones have independent processor state and can be used from separate goroutines as long as the shared source image is not mutated.

Clone does not deep-copy pixels. If you need independent pixel storage, copy the image before constructing processors.

original := gopiq.New(image)
var wg sync.WaitGroup

for range 10 {
    wg.Go(func() {
        processor := original.Clone().
            Resize(100, 100).
            AddTextWatermark("Processed")
        // processor has independent state; its starting image is the shared source.
        if processor.Err() != nil {
            // Handle the processing error.
        }
    })
}
wg.Wait()

docs.title: Concurrent processing pattern
docs.text:
For independent images, create a processor per image. If several processors branch from one base image, use shallow clones and keep the shared source read-only.

func processImagesInParallel(images []image.Image) []*gopiq.ImageProcessor {
    results := make([]*gopiq.ImageProcessor, len(images))
    var wg sync.WaitGroup

    for index, img := range images {
        wg.Go(func() {
            results[index] = gopiq.New(img).
                Resize(200, 200).
                Grayscale()
        })
    }

    wg.Wait()
    return results
}

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Performance depends on image size, CPU, workload, and the selected processing options. No universal speedup is guaranteed; measure your own workload.

docs.title: Benchmark environment
docs.text:
Results below were measured on:

  • Date: 2026-11-01
  • Machine: Apple M1 Pro, 10 logical CPUs
  • OS/architecture: darwin/arm64
  • Go: 1.27.1

Command:

go test -run '^$' \
  -bench 'BenchmarkGrayscale(Small|Medium|Large)_(Optimized|Fast)$|BenchmarkGrayscaleParallelGoroutines$|BenchmarkPipelineAllocations$|BenchmarkConcurrentProcessing$' \
  -benchmem -count=5 .

The tables report the median of five runs. Source images are deterministic RGB patterns generated in performance_test.go; each benchmark creates the processor inside the measured loop while source-image construction is outside the timer. GrayscaleFast() used the default performance options: parallel processing enabled, MaxGoroutines = runtime.NumCPU() (10), and a 10,000-pixel threshold.

docs.title: Grayscale
docs.text:
Image Method Time/op Memory/op Allocs/op Relative to Grayscale 100×100 Grayscale 28.8 µs 41,128 B 4 1.00× 100×100 GrayscaleFast 26.3 µs 41,864 B 25 1.10× 500×500 Grayscale 696.7 µs 1,007,790 B 4 1.00× 500×500 GrayscaleFast 308.6 µs 1,008,530 B 25 2.26× 1920×1080 Grayscale 5.44 ms 8,298,669 B 4 1.00× 1920×1080 GrayscaleFast 1.27 ms 8,299,404 B 25 4.29×

GrayscaleFast has additional goroutine and scheduling overhead for small images. The parallel path becomes more useful as image size increases, but the crossover point depends on the machine and workload.

docs.title: Parallel worker count
docs.text:
1920×1080 image, using GrayscaleFast:

MaxGoroutines Time/op Memory/op Allocs/op 1 5.27 ms 8,298,752 B 7 2 2.91 ms 8,298,827 B 9 4 1.66 ms 8,298,971 B 13 8 1.23 ms 8,299,262 B 21 10 (default) 1.34 ms 8,299,401 B 25 16 1.18 ms 8,299,835 B 37

Using more workers than available CPUs can still change timing, but it also increases allocation and scheduling overhead. Choose a worker count from measurements for the target environment.

docs.title: Pipelines and concurrent processing
docs.text:
Benchmark Time/op Memory/op Allocs/op BenchmarkPipelineAllocations 9.13 ms 12,151,675 B 39 BenchmarkConcurrentProcessing/sequential 16.69 ms 18,556,075 B 35 BenchmarkConcurrentProcessing/parallel 2.43 ms 18,556,075 B 35

BenchmarkPipelineAllocations measures creating two clones and running grayscale, fast grayscale, and resize on an 800×600 source. BenchmarkConcurrentProcessing measures resize, fast grayscale, and crop on a 1000×1000 source, both sequentially and through parallel b.RunParallel execution.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
opts := gopiq.PerformanceOptions{
    MaxGoroutines:            8,
    EnableParallelProcessing: true,
    MinSizeForParallel:       10000,
}

processor := gopiq.NewWithPerformanceOptions(image, opts)

The default options enable parallel processing at 10,000 pixels and use runtime.NumCPU() goroutines. A MaxGoroutines value less than or equal to zero uses that runtime default; a MinSizeForParallel value less than or equal to zero allows parallel processing for any non-empty image. GrayscaleFast() leaves empty images unchanged, and disabling parallel processing always selects the sequential path.

docs.title: Implementation facts
docs.text:
• Grayscale conversion uses direct RGBA buffer access and the BT.709 luma calculation.
  • GrayscaleFast() uses parallel row workers when enabled and above the configured threshold.
  • The library does not currently implement image-buffer pooling or SIMD kernels, and this page makes no claims for them.

docs.title: gopiq Roadmap
docs.text: This roadmap turns the specification into ordered, verifiable milestones. It is dependency-ordered, not calendar-based; no dates or delivery estimates are implied. Milestones are Planned unless marked Complete.

docs.title: M0 — Make the repository buildable
docs.text:
Status: Complete · Priority: P0 · Requirements: BLD-1–BLD-3

  • Move each standalone example into an independently buildable package/directory, or use an equivalent layout that avoids duplicate main functions.
  • Correct example asset paths and run instructions after reorganizing.
  • Keep generated example output separate from tracked input fixtures.
  • Ensure the CI build/test commands cover the resulting package layout.

Exit criteria: go build ./... and go test ./... both complete successfully, and each documented example can be built independently.

docs.title: M1 — Correct core image processing and guard edge cases
docs.text:
Status: Complete · Priority: P1 · Requirements: IMG-1–IMG-5, GRAY-1–GRAY-5, SAFE-1–SAFE-3

  • Fix parallel grayscale indexing for non-zero-origin bounds and subimages.
  • Handle empty images and performance-option edge cases without zero-worker division or invalid pixel access.
  • Verify exact grayscale agreement between sequential and parallel paths, including alpha.
  • Check crop coordinate arithmetic and image-buffer size calculations before use or allocation.
  • Define and test empty-source behavior for crop, resize, grayscale, and watermarking.

Exit criteria: Regression tests cover zero-origin and non-zero-origin images, subimages, empty bounds, alpha, and invalid/overflowing dimensions; invalid inputs report chain errors rather than arithmetic-driven panics.

docs.title: M2 — Make watermark and format behavior match the API
docs.text:
Status: Complete · Priority: P1 · Requirements: WM-1–WM-5, FMT-1–FMT-4

  • Implement WithFontPath and deterministic font-source option ordering.
  • Validate nil/invalid watermark options and calculate all positions relative to image bounds.
  • Register GIF decoding in the library and retain an explicit error for unsupported GIF encoding.
  • Add tests for font files, option errors, anchor positions, non-zero bounds, and JPEG/PNG/GIF behavior.

Exit criteria: Every advertised option has observable behavior or is removed; format conversion and errors match the specification.

docs.title: M3 — Resolve clone and concurrency semantics
docs.text:
Status: Complete · Priority: P1 · Requirements: CON-1–CON-5

  • Make Go docs, README, tests, and concurrency docs consistently describe Clone as shallow.
  • Document that input and returned images are read-only during concurrent processing.
  • Clarify that individual method calls are synchronized but a multi-call chain is not atomic.
  • Replace or extend the current race test so readers and state-changing operations act on the same processor.

Exit criteria: The public contract is consistent across code and docs, and go test -race ./... covers the stated concurrency guarantee.

docs.title: M4 — Establish reliable quality gates and truthful performance docs
docs.text:
Status: Complete · Priority: P1 · Requirements: BLD-4, Q-1–Q-6

  • Move timing comparisons out of regular tests and into benchmarks or a separately invoked tool.
  • Decide whether the unused RGBA pool is worth implementing; remove it and its claims if measurements do not support it.
  • Remove or substantiate SIMD and fixed speedup claims with reproducible benchmark data.
  • Add regression coverage for the requirements in M1–M3.
  • Run build, tests, race detection, vet, lint, and documentation build in CI; retain Go 1.27.0 as the declared minimum unless the policy is deliberately changed.

Exit criteria: Ordinary tests are correctness-focused and stable across machines; all release-gate checks in the specification pass.

docs.title: M5 — Add a standalone CLI
docs.text:
Priority: P2 · Requirements: CLI-1–CLI-5

  • Add a thin cmd/gopiq entry point and testable command logic under internal/cli.
  • Implement convert, resize, crop, grayscale, and watermark commands with help and version output.
  • Support file and standard input/output, format inference and --format, clear GIF-output errors, documented exit codes, and safe output writes.
  • Add command integration tests, CLI documentation, Makefile build/install targets, and coverage reporting for the CLI package.
  • Keep the CLI dependent only on the public root package; do not import internal/engine directly.

Exit criteria: The CLI builds and installs, every command and documented flag is covered by tests, format and exit-code behavior matches the specification, CLI documentation is published, and CI passes.

docs.title: M6 — Add streaming I/O and decode limits
docs.text:
Priority: P2 · Requirements: EXT-1, EXT-2

  • Design reader-based construction and writer-based encoding while keeping FromBytes and ToBytes compatible.
  • Add configurable encoded-size, dimension, and total-pixel limits, validating before full decode where possible.
  • Document defaults, limit errors, ownership, and resource behavior.

Exit criteria: Streaming callers avoid mandatory full encoded-buffer copies, and configured decode limits are enforced by tests including oversized and malformed inputs.

docs.title: M7 — Expand transformation and format capabilities
docs.text:
Priority: P2 · Requirements: EXT-3–EXT-5

  • Specify proportional resize fit/fill behavior, including rounding, crop, and upscaling rules.
  • Evaluate rotation, flips, and image watermarks with bounds and alpha-compositing semantics.
  • Assess additional formats independently; implement GIF output only after choosing and documenting palette quantization.

Exit criteria: Each selected feature has a written API contract, pixel-level tests, and documentation before implementation is considered complete.

docs.title: M8 — Optimize measured workloads and support bounded batches
docs.text:
Priority: P3 · Requirements: EXT-6–EXT-8

  • Benchmark representative image sizes and processor counts; tune parallel thresholds based on reproducible results.
  • Consider pooling, fixed-point arithmetic, SIMD, or other specialized paths only when profiling justifies them.
  • Design bounded batch processing with explicit ordering, concurrency, and cancellation semantics.
  • Expand fuzz, platform, and Go-version coverage according to the declared support policy.

Exit criteria: Optimizations show a repeatable benefit without changing specified output semantics, and batch/resource behavior is bounded and tested.

docs.title: Cross-milestone rules
docs.text:
• Fixes must include regression tests and keep error propagation consistent with the chain API.
  • Do not claim an optimization or format is supported until implementation and tests demonstrate it.
  • Avoid calendar commitments until scope and maintainer capacity are known.
  • A release is gated by the acceptance criteria in the specification, not by completion of every future extension.

docs.title: gopiq Specification
docs.text:
Status: Draft implementation target · Scope: Correctness, safety, supported formats, concurrency, verification, and planned extensions

This document defines the intended behavior of gopiq and the acceptance criteria for fixing the gaps found in the repository audit. “Must” and “must not” are requirements; “should” indicates a recommended implementation choice.

docs.title: 1. Goals
docs.text:
gopiq must provide a predictable, chainable image-processing API that:

  • builds and tests as a complete Go module, including its examples;
  • handles ordinary and non-zero-origin image bounds without panicking;
  • reports invalid operations through the processor error chain;
  • has clear, testable format and concurrency guarantees; and
  • makes performance claims only when supported by reproducible measurements.

The Go 1.27.0 minimum is part of this specification. The CI matrix checks that minimum and the latest supported Go 1.27 patch release.

docs.title: 2. Audit baseline and resolution status
docs.text:
The initial audit found the following gaps. M0–M4 have resolved all listed items.

  • Resolved in M0: Standalone examples previously redeclared main in one package, breaking go build ./... and go test ./...; they now build independently.
  • Resolved in M1: Parallel grayscale previously mishandled non-zero-origin bounds, and empty images or unsafe dimensions could reach invalid operations.
  • Resolved in M2: WithFontPath previously had no effect; font-source ordering and option validation are now implemented.
  • Resolved in M2: GIF was described as decodable but its decoder was not registered by the library.
  • Resolved in M3: Clone is now documented and tested as a shallow copy, and the concurrency contract covers per-call synchronization, non-atomic chains, and read-only images.
  • Resolved in M4: The unused RGBA pool and unsupported pooling/SIMD claims were removed; performance documentation now reports measured benchmarks with environment and workload details.
  • Resolved in M4: Timing comparisons were removed from ordinary tests and performance measurement now lives in benchmarks.

docs.title: 3.1 Build, examples, and documentation
docs.text:
• BLD-1: Every Go package in the module must compile under go build ./... and go test ./....
  • BLD-2: Each standalone example must be in its own package/directory (or an equivalent structure that avoids duplicate main declarations). Example instructions must work from the documented working directory.
  • BLD-3: Building examples must not require running them or writing generated images into tracked fixture locations.
  • BLD-4: The MkDocs site must build with the documented requirements, and the specification and roadmap must be discoverable in its navigation.

docs.title: 3.2 Image operations and bounds
docs.text:
• IMG-1: Crop(x, y, width, height) interprets x and y in the source image's coordinate space. The crop rectangle must have positive dimensions, fit within the source bounds, and be computed without integer overflow. The resulting image has bounds starting at (0, 0).
  • IMG-2: Resize(width, height) requires positive target dimensions and produces a zero-origin image of the requested size. Invalid or unrepresentable buffer sizes must become chain errors rather than arithmetic-driven panics.
  • IMG-3: Operations must support valid images whose bounds do not start at (0, 0), including subimages. Pixel loops must use coordinates or offsets appropriate to the image's actual bounds and stride.
  • IMG-4: Operations on empty bounds must have documented behavior and must not panic. Grayscale operations on an empty image are a no-op that preserves its bounds. Crop, resize, and text-watermark operations on an empty image report a chain error because they cannot produce a valid result.
  • IMG-5: Processing operations must not mutate the source image in place.

docs.title: 3.3 Grayscale and performance options
docs.text:
• GRAY-1: Grayscale and GrayscaleFast must support arbitrary valid bounds and subimages without out-of-range buffer access.
  • GRAY-2: Both methods must use the same documented BT.709 luma calculation and produce identical pixel values for the same input. For the current 8-bit RGBA implementation, the calculation is uint8(0.2126*R + 0.7152*G + 0.0722*B); output RGB channels are equal and alpha is preserved.
  • GRAY-3: Parallel work must use at least one worker only when there are rows to process, and no more workers than rows or the configured maximum. Empty images must never reach a division by zero.
  • GRAY-4: MaxGoroutines <= 0 uses the documented runtime default. MinSizeForParallel <= 0 means no minimum threshold for a non-empty image; it must not make empty-image processing unsafe. EnableParallelProcessing == false always selects the sequential path.
  • GRAY-5: Default options and threshold behavior must be documented and tested. SetPerformanceOptions must remain safe to call concurrently with processor methods.

docs.title: 3.4 Watermarks
docs.text:
• WM-1: Font-source options are applied in order: the last supplied WithFontPath or WithFontBytes option selects the source. With neither option, the embedded Go font is used.
  • WM-2: WithFontPath must load and parse the requested file. File-read, parse, and face-construction failures must be returned through the processor error chain.
  • WM-3: Empty text, a nil option, a nil color, a non-finite, non-positive, or renderer-unrepresentable font size, non-finite offsets, and an unknown position must produce a processor error rather than a panic or silent fallback. Offsets are anchor-relative: positive offsets inset corner anchors and move center-anchored text right/down; negative finite offsets remain valid and may move text partly outside the image.
  • WM-4: Named positions are calculated relative to the image bounds, including non-zero Min coordinates. Text outside the destination is clipped by drawing; it is not silently repositioned.
  • WM-5: Watermarking must preserve the source image and must be covered by tests for each anchor, custom fonts, errors, and non-zero-origin bounds.

docs.title: 3.5 Formats
docs.text:
• FMT-1: JPEG and PNG decoding and encoding remain supported and covered by round-trip tests.
  • FMT-2: GIF decoding is supported independently of whether the importing application imports image/gif; the library registers the decoder itself.
  • FMT-3: GIF encoding remains unsupported until a palette-quantization policy is selected. Calls to encode GIF must return a clear error, not imply successful support.
  • FMT-4: FormatFromString, ImageFormat.String, and format comments must agree with the formats actually accepted for decoding and encoding.

docs.title: 3.6 Error handling and size safety
docs.text:
• SAFE-1: Chainable operations preserve the first error and do not continue processing after it. Export methods return that error.
  • SAFE-2: Crop arithmetic and image-buffer size calculations must be checked for integer overflow before use or allocation.
  • SAFE-3: Invalid dimensions and configuration must return errors through the existing API. The library is not required to recover from operating-system out-of-memory termination.
  • SAFE-4: Decoding limits for encoded bytes, dimensions, and total pixels are a planned extension; callers must not be told that untrusted input is resource-bounded until those limits exist.

docs.title: 3.7 Concurrency and cloning contract
docs.text:
To preserve current behavior and avoid an implicit full-image copy, the v1 Clone contract is shallow:

  • CON-1: Clone copies processor state and performance options but shares the current image reference. Go documentation, README, tests, and concurrency docs must say this; they must not call it a deep copy or promise independent backing pixels.
  • CON-2: Processing operations treat their input image as read-only and create a new destination. Clones can therefore process the shared source independently as long as the source is not externally mutated.
  • CON-3: Methods on one processor must be internally race-safe. Individual calls are synchronized, but a multi-call chain is not an atomic transaction and may interleave with calls from another goroutine.
  • CON-4: Image() returns the current image for reading. The caller must treat it, and images passed to constructors, as read-only while the processor or its clones may be used concurrently. Mutating an image through a concrete-type assertion is outside the thread-safety guarantee.
  • CON-5: Race tests must exercise concurrent reads and state-changing calls on the same processor, not only writes to separate clones.

If independent pixel storage is later needed, it should be provided by an explicitly named deep-copy API rather than changing the meaning of Clone silently.

docs.title: 3.8 Tests, CI, and performance claims
docs.text:
• Q-1: CI must build and test all packages, run the race detector, and include go vet and the configured linter. It must build the documentation site.
  • Q-2: Tests must cover non-zero-origin images, subimages, empty bounds, alpha preservation, grayscale equivalence, invalid sizes/options, font-path loading, and the declared format behavior.
  • Q-3: Timing comparisons belong in Go benchmarks or a separately invoked performance tool, not ordinary unit tests. Unit tests must not depend on machine speed.
  • Q-4: Benchmark results must include enough environment and workload detail to be reproduced. Documentation must not present old measurements as universal guarantees.
  • Q-5: Pooling or SIMD optimizations may be claimed only when the implementation uses them and reproducible benchmarks demonstrate a benefit. Otherwise, unused pool code and unsupported claims should be removed.
  • Q-6: The supported Go-version policy must be explicit. CI must test the module's declared minimum (currently Go 1.27.0) and the latest supported stable patch release in that Go line.

docs.title: 3.9 Command-line interface
docs.text:
• CLI-1: The module must provide a cmd/gopiq main package that builds with go build ./cmd/gopiq and installs with go install github.com/TamasGorgics/gopiq/cmd/gopiq@latest. Command parsing and execution logic must live in a testable internal package rather than in main.
  • CLI-2: The CLI must provide documented convert, resize, crop, grayscale, and watermark commands, plus help and version output. Required arguments, optional flags, and operation semantics must match the public library API.
  • CLI-3: The CLI must read input from a file or standard input and write output to a file or standard output. Output format is inferred from the destination extension when possible and may be overridden with --format. JPEG, PNG, and GIF input are supported; JPEG and PNG output are supported; GIF output must return a clear unsupported error.
  • CLI-4: Usage and flag errors must return exit code 2; input, processing, encoding, and write errors must return exit code 1; success, help, and version output must return exit code 0. Errors must be written to standard error. Failed output writes must not leave a truncated destination when an atomic write can be used.
  • CLI-5: The CLI must use only the supported root package and the standard library, not the internal engine directly. Tests must cover every command, format inference and overrides, standard input/output, invalid arguments, unsupported GIF output, exit codes, and output-write failure behavior; CLI usage must be documented in the MkDocs site and linked from the README.

docs.title: 4. Planned extensions
docs.text:
These are not prerequisites for the correctness milestones above; they are future capabilities to consider and scope separately.

  • EXT-1 — Streaming I/O: Add reader-based construction and writer-based encoding so callers need not hold the entire encoded image in a byte slice. Existing byte APIs remain supported wrappers.
  • EXT-2 — Decode limits: Add configurable limits for encoded input size, width, height, and total pixels, with validation before full decode where possible.
  • EXT-3 — Aspect-ratio operations: Add explicit fit/fill or proportional-resize APIs with documented rounding, cropping, and upscaling behavior.
  • EXT-4 — Additional operations: Consider rotation, flips, and image watermarks with clear bounds, anchor, and alpha-compositing behavior.
  • EXT-5 — Additional formats: Consider GIF encoding only with an explicit quantization policy; assess additional formats and dependencies independently.
  • EXT-6 — Bounded batch processing: Consider a worker-pool API with bounded concurrency, ordering guarantees, and cancellation behavior for batch workloads.
  • EXT-7 — Benchmark-led optimization: Profile representative workloads before adding pooling, fixed-point arithmetic, SIMD, or other specialized paths. Keep a simple correct fallback.
  • EXT-8 — Expanded assurance: Add fuzzing for malformed image data and options, broader platform/version CI, and automated checks that documentation examples stay compilable.

docs.title: 5. Release acceptance gate
docs.text:
A release implementing the corrective requirements is ready when all of the following hold:

  1. go build ./... and go test ./... pass.
  2. go test -race ./..., go vet ./..., and the configured linter pass.
  3. The MkDocs site builds and all example instructions work as written.
  4. Requirements in sections 3.2–3.8 have regression tests or an explicit documented exception. The CLI requirements in section 3.9 apply to releases that ship the CLI.
  5. Performance documentation describes measured behavior without unsupported guarantees.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This section covers the core methods for creating and managing ImageProcessor instances.

  • New(img image.Image) *ImageProcessor - Create processor from image; the image is retained, not copied
  • FromBytes(data []byte) *ImageProcessor - Decode JPEG, PNG, or GIF bytes into a processor
  • Clone() *ImageProcessor - Create a shallow processor copy; error and performance state are copied, image storage is shared
  • Image() (image.Image, error) - Get the current image for reading
  • ToBytes(format ImageFormat) ([]byte, error) - Export to bytes
  • Err() error - Get any error from the processing chain

Methods are individually synchronized, but a multi-call chain is not atomic. Images passed to New and images returned by Image must be treated as read-only while the processor or its clones may be used concurrently. Clone does not deep-copy pixels.

ToBytes supports JPEG and PNG output. GIF is decode-only; attempting to encode GIF returns an error.

docs.title: Processing Operations
docs.text:
These methods are chainable and perform image manipulation.

  • Resize(width, height int) - Resize a non-empty image using Catmull-Rom interpolation; invalid or unrepresentable sizes set a chain error.
  • Crop(x, y, width, height int) - Crop using source-image coordinates; the result has zero-origin bounds.
  • Grayscale() - Convert to grayscale; empty images are left unchanged.
  • GrayscaleFast() - Convert to grayscale using parallel processing when enabled and above the configured threshold; empty images are left unchanged.
  • AddTextWatermark(text, ...options) - Add text watermark; an empty destination image returns a chain error.

Crop and resize reject invalid dimensions. Cropping uses absolute coordinates from the source image bounds and returns a chain error for empty bounds. Resizing an image with empty bounds also returns a chain error.

All operations treat their source image as read-only. When they succeed on non-empty input, they create a new destination image. Do not mutate an image passed to New or returned by Image while the processor or its clones may be used concurrently.

docs.title: Watermark Options
docs.text:
Use these functional options to customize text watermarks.

  • WithFontPath(path string) - Load a .ttf or .otf font file.
  • WithFontBytes(data []byte) - Use font data directly.
  • WithFontSize(size float64) - Set a finite, positive font size within the renderer's fixed-point range.
  • WithColor(color color.Color) - Set a non-nil text color.
  • WithPosition(pos WatermarkPosition) - Select one of the five named anchors.
  • WithOffset(x, y float64) - Set finite pixel offsets. Positive values inset corner anchors; at the center they move right/down. Negative values are allowed and can move text outside the image.

The last supplied font-source option (WithFontPath or WithFontBytes) wins. If neither is supplied, gopiq uses its embedded Go font. A missing or invalid font, invalid option, empty text, or empty destination image sets the processor's chain error.

Named positions are calculated relative to the image bounds, including non-zero origins. Text that extends beyond the image is clipped rather than moved back into view. Watermarking draws onto a copy and leaves the source image unchanged.
